messages.subject: Advices on mesh building
parts:
Good evening,

I'm to work on a replicated point pattern and our study area is divided
into 6 different zones.
What are the rules I should respect when building the mesh, in order to
obtain a proper estimation for the spatial effect across our study area
(for a space-time Log-cox process).
In case it's of any help, the shapefile can be downloaded here:
https://www.dropbox.com/s/5m0ogrxwahf416b/StudyArea.zip?dl=0

Thanks in advance for your advices.

Alex

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Advices on mesh building
parts:
Hi Alex,

You have a set of of disconnected regions and want a model such that the
process into each region is treated as replicas. The easier way to do
it is to build a mesh that has nodes only inside each of these regions.
You can include outer extension by adding a buffer into each region
before running the following commands.

require(rgdal)
map <- readOGR('./', 'SA_LB_PCsimple_L93')

require(INLA)
bound <- inla.sp2segment(map)
(el <- mean(apply(bbox(map), 1, function(x) 0.03*diff(x))))
(mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary=bound, max.edge=el))$n

plot(map)
plot(mesh, add=TRUE)

Elias
